critical_code_review_comments: graph_builder.py is correctly token-economical: prior_blob_shas is loaded from project_graphs, changed_top = [p for p in top if blob_shas.get(p) != prior_blob_shas.get(p)], and the LLM describe call is gated on `if changed_top:` — confirmed by static asserts in test_build_graph_skips_llm_when_no_changes. For an unchanged repo the build does zero LLM calls and reuses prior_descriptions.get(path, '') in the regex pass.

cto_projects.py — every graph endpoint pattern is: me = await current_dev(authorization); user_id = me['user_id']; then graph read filtered by {project_id, user_id}. This is the same compound-key pattern used by get_graph(), so a project_id owned by User A cannot be read with User B's bearer (the find_one returns None → endpoint returns {status:'not_built'} without ever touching User A's row). Confirmed live: founder bearer + unowned project_id → status:'not_built'.
POST /graph/impact correctly returns HTTPException(400, 'files[] required') when body.files is missing or empty — verified live (HTTP 400 with that exact detail).

Frontend Dashboard.jsx onTabChange (lines 324-343) cleanly dispatches `aurem:toggle-graph` with {open:true} when tab === 'Graph' and {open:false} when returning to Chat — symmetric open/close contract. ChatPanel.jsx listens once at line 670 and toggles graphOpen flag → GraphPanel mounts/unmounts. No regressions in topbar focus mode / autohide.

Minor harness note (not a code issue): Playwright `.click(force=True)` on the Graph tab did NOT consistently fire the React synthetic onClick handler — but a JS-dispatched HTMLElement.click() did, AND real user mouse clicks fire it correctly. This is a test-harness pointer-interception quirk, not a UI bug; the React tree responds normally to native click events as a real user would generate.
